items.note: Story 1: Association named, organized 1889 at Larrow Green, Gideon Vose first president, creamery built 1891 — all four present.
Article VII quoted verbatim: paid by pounds of butterfat ascertained by test, not by weight of milk; test of the station where he delivers governs.
Story 1 states the rule is why the trouble turned on it — it made each station's own test equipment, with no cross-check, the sole basis of every patron's pay.
Only Hobart Sill (buttermaker) appears anywhere in Section A. No Effie Loomis, no Wilbur Teague.
Selby Vose never appears in Section A. Named only at B3/B4, and there dated manager from 1911 (a planted error). Section B cannot travel into A.
No station-gain ledger line in Section A. The 5.25 percent ledger note appears only at C1(a), which cannot travel into A.
Story 2: Ostrey Hollow, seven miles up the valley, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, glassware borrowed from Larrow Green (Sill's outfit).

Section A gives only 'weighed, tested, separated on the spot; cream hauled down, skim home'. No composite sample, no percent read on the graduated neck, no fixed charge from the pipette. The mechanism appears only at C1(a).
Ammon & Sons invoice of 14 April 1897, outfit in use from 1 May 1897 — the correct date, chosen over the 1898/1899 variants.
Six dozen milk-test pipettes marked 17.6 cc, twelve dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, line items summing to $77.93. The $77.39 variant is attributed to one source, not adopted.
Section A never states the shortfall was flat at 0.19 in every month of every year. The 'constant in every month' claim sits at C1(b), outside Section A.
Nothing on the pipette being uncheckable without a burette, and no burette in the county.

Ansel Keddie appointed tester the day the station opened (1896), held the post twenty-nine seasons until 1925. Service and its end given; the 30 April date is missing but the item bundles without a REQUIRED line.
The test book is never mentioned in Section A — no bench routine, no columns, no crossed-and-initialed corrections.
No summary leaf in Section A. The 3.61/3.80 pair appears only at C1(b).
The 1911 interval is named once in the framing list of eight episodes and never reconstructed — no 8 May, no 10 July, no 3.80, no question mark.
Orra is identified as the tester's wife, but Section A never states she was a Brant or Emmet's sister. Both bolded elements are required; the sibling link is only speculated at B2.
Section A only says the matter 'stayed closed until 1919 — a later story'. No circular, no manager's signature, no 17 March 1925 statement.
No death in 1934, no impounding of the book, no county historical rooms.

Granddaughter, correct (+1). Derivation point lost: the run never states Ivy is Duncan Keddie's daughter and Duncan is Ansel's son — it rests entirely on Falke's self-correction and explicitly calls the intervening generation an open gap.

'Most likely second cousins' with a workable derivation through Roy and Duncan as first cousins (+1). Abstention item A08 lost: the run never raises whether Emmet and Orra were full or half siblings, so it does not state that this cannot be determined and does not change the answer. No -2, since it asserts neither.

Gideon Vose, his father, correctly resolved against the 'nephew' variant (+1). Significance (+1): the run states, at B4 within scope, that Gideon wrote the by-law making a station's own test the basis of pay and that his son signed the 1919 watering circular and presided over Keddie's dismissal, 'running through Gideon Vose's own Article VII'.

Correct abstention on A01 — verdict sentence is qualified ('none that the sources establish') and closes 'cannot be determined from the sources... silence isn't proof of absence'. No -2. Second point lost: the run says 'none is claimed anywhere', missing what is established — two narrators assert a cousinship from talk, one denies it flatly, and no document names or denies a link.

0.95 / 5.00 percent short, matching the key. Working is backwards and wrong on the record — the run claims the sources give no pipette calibration figure, when 16.72 c.c. is documented — but the value is exact.
True average 3.80, recorded short by 0.19. Exact.

Answers $19,600 and 19.4 percent. The key requires $19,000 and 20 percent / one fifth. The run computed $19,000 correctly and then overrode it with the planted $19,600, inverting which figure the sources support.
Declines the whole of C2 as undeterminable. Key: 200,000 x 3.42% = 6,840 lb. C2 is not an abstention item.
Not attempted. Key: true test 3.60, true fat 7,200 lb, owed 360 lb.
Not attempted. Key: 360 x $0.24 = $86.40.

deductions.reason: Planted error asserted as fact: 'Selby Vose became the Association's manager in 1911' (B3), repeated at B4. Canon: 1913 (corruption-map X94).
Planted error asserted as fact: the shortfall was worth '$19,600' (C1d), adopted as the run's own answer over its own correct $19,000. Corruption-map X41/X74, NT-8.
